title: Structural Polymer Group, Ltd. v. Zoltek Corp.
summary: Good-faith requirements and a price-matching mechanism made the supply arrangement binding despite variable demand and a year with no purchases.
notes:
Court: Eighth Circuit (2008).

The notes connect requirements and output contracts to UCC § 2-306 and ask when cessation or a sharp change in quantities reflects good faith. They do not state that every zero order or every output change is permissible.

sections.Parties: Structural Polymer Group and its related purchasing business sought carbon fiber from Zoltek under a long-term requirements arrangement.
sections.Material Facts: The agreement ran from late 2000 through 2010 and governed large-tow carbon fiber. Requirements changed over time, including a year without purchases. The buyer could respond to a competing lower price, but Zoltek had a contractual opportunity to match it. The dispute involved Zoltek’s failure to meet later demand and disagreements over covered products.
sections.Procedural History: The case reached the Eighth Circuit after a jury verdict. The award was reduced from $36,044,895 to $21,138,518 to avoid recovery on alternative theories for the same loss. The appellate court affirmed the reduced judgment.
sections.Issue: Was the requirements promise illusory because the buyer’s quantity could vary, and did the alternative-price provision let the buyer escape its obligation at will?
sections.Holding: The agreement was enforceable. Good-faith requirements constrained quantity, and the price-matching provision did not provide an unrestricted right to buy elsewhere. The reduced award was affirmed.
sections.Reasoning: A requirements arrangement commits the buyer’s actual good-faith demand rather than a fixed numerical amount. A period of zero demand does not, without more, show the absence of an obligation. If Zoltek matched the competing price, the agreement continued to constrain the buyer’s source of supply. The court reads the provisions together rather than isolate one discretionary phrase. The disposition also separates alternative legal theories from duplicative monetary recovery.
